gaps.sentence: The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: The course offers not only theory ___ hands-on fieldwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only... but also' is the fixed correlative pair.

gaps.sentence: He didn't whisper the news; ___, he announced it to the whole office.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' corrects the first statement with its opposite.

gaps.sentence: He whispered ___ the children wouldn't hear.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + wouldn't' expresses intended (here negative) purpose.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was fully booked. ___, we found a room at a guesthouse nearby.
gaps.explanation: Finding a room contradicts the expected failure: However signals the contrast.

gaps.sentence: The economy has strengthened; ___, unemployment keeps rising.
gaps.explanation: Rising unemployment goes against the positive trend: however marks the contrast.
